div.head: II Cn 73.1
div.ab: ⁊ si he his weres scyldig wið þone cingc oððe wið þone, þe he his socne geunnen hæbbe.
⁊ sy he his weres scyldig wið þonne cyngc oððe wið þonne, þe he hit geunnan hæbbe.
Et sit ipse maritus werę suę reus erga regem, uel cui rex concesserit.
⁊ si he his] weres scyldig wið ðone kyning oððe wið ðone ðe he hit geunnen hæbbe.
And he (the second husband) shall forfeit his wergeld to the king or to the lord to whom it has been granted.
And he is to be liable to pay his wergild to the king or to him to whom he has granted it.
Und der [zweite Mann] sei sein Wergeld schuldig an den König oder an den, dem dieser es (Gerichtsbarkeit über ihn G) gewährt hat.
And let the [second husband] be liable for his wergild to the king or to the one to whom the king has granted it (jurisdiction over him, G).
div.note: Liebermann thinks ‘hit’ (in the other MSS) more original than G's ‘his socne’; compare II Cn 63.
i.e. the right of private jurisdiction
